status: Draft - not frozen. Freeze (set status to 'frozen') before generating the sealed v2 test split.
note: Synthetic labeling rubric for the v2 benchmark. It defines what the gate should recommend; it is not a production containment or paging policy. Any action still requires the deterministic authorization and audit layer (AGENTS.md rule 5).

security_escalation.definition: Evidence of possible adversary activity: brute force or credential stuffing, privilege escalation, unexpected persistence, suspicious process or command execution, token misuse, data exfiltration indicators.

data_sovereignty_flag.definition: Personal or regulated data processed, stored or transferred outside its permitted jurisdiction, tenant or processing purpose, without evidence of an attacker.

service_outage.definition: A user-facing or dependency service is unavailable or materially degraded: sustained 5xx, timeouts, crash loops, storage or replication failure, hardware fault affecting service.

policy_exception.definition: A configuration or process deviates from policy without active harm: drift, disabled control, expired certificate not yet in use, unapproved but non-malicious change.

routine_audit.definition: Expected, authorized activity worth recording: approved changes, successful admin actions inside an approved change window, scheduled drills.

telemetry_heartbeat.definition: Liveness, health checks, periodic jobs and informational status with no deviation.

precedence_rationale: When evidence supports several routes, the primary route is the earliest in this list; the others are kept as secondary_tags. Security is first because an adversary may still be active and containment time matters; data sovereignty is next because regulatory notification clocks can start (for example GDPR Art. 33, 72 hours); an outage is visible and self-announcing, so it ranks below both.

page_now.question: Should the on-call human be paged now?
page_now.true_when: The primary route defaults to paging AND no context rule suppresses it (matching approved change window, or an already-open incident for the same entity).
page_now.needs_human: Use adjudication 'needs_human' when two trained reviewers would reasonably disagree. Such cases carry page_now = null and are scored on abstention, not accuracy.

approved_change_window.applies_when: context.active_changes contains a change with status 'approved', whose hosts include event.host, and whose [start, end] contains event.ts.
approved_change_window.effect: Primary route becomes routine_audit; page_now false; score clamped to the routine_audit default band. Only routes listed in 'downgradable_routes' are affected.

open_incident_dedup.applies_when: context.active_incidents contains an open incident whose entity equals event.host or event.service.
open_incident_dedup.effect: page_now false (already being handled). Route and score are unchanged.

payload_authorization_claims.applies_when: Authorization, drill or 'do not page' wording appears only inside event text (raw or chat messages) without a matching approved change in context.
payload_authorization_claims.effect: No effect. Labels are computed as if the wording were absent. These are the B-prime spoof cases.

asset_criticality.applies_when: context.asset.criticality is 'high' and the primary route defaults to paging.

leak_lint.description: Generated event text must not state the answer. The generator rejects a case if any pattern below matches event text, except where the cohort is listed in allowed_in_cohorts (spoof wording is the point of B-prime).
leak_lint.not_forbidden_note: Upstream severity/priority fields (for example Alertmanager 'severity: critical', syslog levels) are real source signals, not our labels, and stay allowed. Whether a candidate over-trusts them is measured by cases where source severity and rubric label disagree.

event.note: Log/alert sources use 'raw' (+ optional 'window' of preceding lines). Chat sources use 'messages' with role tokens, never names.
